# Motion, actions and transitions

Frame Job has three ways to make a clip move or change over time. An **action** animates a clip's properties from one state to another over a span you choose: a zoom into a screen recording, a fade of the volume, a title that slides and changes colour. **Motion presets** give a clip a ready-made entrance, exit or continuous movement that stays tied to the clip's two ends. A **transition** plays where two clips on one track overlap. This page covers all three, and what the Clip tab shows while you work on an action.

## Actions

An action is a span of time on one clip. Over that span, the clip's properties ease from whatever they were when the span began to the action's **end state**, along the action's curve. When the span is over, the clip holds the end state until a later action changes it again.

- An action's times are measured from the clip's own start (clip time), not from the start of the timeline.
- Actions on one clip may not overlap. A clip can have as many actions as fit end to end.
- Several actions run in time order. Each one starts from the state the earlier ones left behind.
- A new action's end state is empty, so it changes nothing until you edit it.

### How values change over an action

| Kind of value | What happens over the span |
|---|---|
| Numbers (position, scale, rotation, opacity, crop, volume, a filter's amount, a grade's sliders, a graphic's number properties) | Ramp along the action's curve |
| Colours (shadow, chroma key, text colours, word-caption colours, a graphic's colour properties) | Ramp in OKLab, which keeps the blend's midpoints even. A colour whose two ends are equal stays exact |
| Switches, popups and text (an on/off box, a filter's kind, a font, a graphic's string, boolean or image property) | Hold, then switch to the end value when the action ends |
| Lists (filters, obscure regions) | Ramp entry by entry while both ends have the same number of entries. If the list's length changes, the whole list switches at the end. If one entry changes kind (or a region its shape), only that entry switches at the end and the others still ramp |
| Curves | Always animate. Two curves with the same number of points ramp point by point; a neutral curve lines up with the other curve's points; two curves with different numbers of points blend their values over the action |

The four curves are the same everywhere an action or a transition is eased:

| Curve | Lane label | Feel |
|---|---|---|
| Linear | Linear | Constant speed |
| Ease In | In | Starts slowly, ends fast |
| Ease Out | Out | Starts fast, ends slowly |
| Ease In Out | In Out | Slow at both ends |

A new action from **Add Action** is **Linear**. A zoom action is **Ease In Out**.

### What an action can animate

- **Picture.** Everything in the Picture sub-tab that is a value: transform, opacity, crop, corner radius, shadow, reflection, spotlight, the amounts inside filters and obscure regions. See [Canvas and layers](canvas-and-layers.md).
- **Color.** Light, Colour, Wheels, Curves, Look amount and, on an adjustment clip, Strength and the Qualifier. See [Color grading](color-grading.md).
- **Sound.** The Sound sub-tab's Volume and Fades sections. See [Audio](audio.md).
- **Text.** The Text sub-tab's style, size and colours. See [Captions](captions.md) for word captions.
- **Graphics.** A graphic clip's properties. Numbers and colours ramp; strings, booleans, choices and images switch at the end. A property the graphic marks as not animatable cannot be put in an action. See [Graphics](graphics.md).
- **Speed.** A media clip's playback rate, which makes a speed ramp. See [Speed](speed.md).

Some things are never animated. These rows write the clip itself, whatever is selected, and are marked ⊘ in the Clip tab:

- The Motion presets section (below).
- In the Sound sub-tab: Ducking, the fade shapes, the Voice Effect, and a nest clip's Mix to mono. Every other audio setting animates ([Audio](audio.md#animating-the-sound)).
- In the Clip sub-tab's Speed section: Keep pitch and Fit to.
- **Adding or removing** a filter or an obscure region. Changing a value inside an existing entry still animates.
- A shape's own properties in the Shape sub-tab (its kind, stroke, fill, gradient and arrows). Its position, scale and opacity animate like any clip's.
### Select an action

An action is selected when you:

- click its band in the timeline or in the Clip tab's action lane,
- add it (with Add Action, Zoom to Region or Zoom Back), or
- play or scrub the playhead **into** its span while its clip is the only one selected.

Clicking a band on a clip that is part of a multi-clip selection selects just that clip and its action.

Clicking a band also moves the playhead to the action's end, so the preview shows the state the Clip tab is editing (one frame short when the action ends with the clip).

Leaving the span keeps the action selected. To leave it, press **Esc**, click the **Clip** chip at the start of the action lane, or select a different clip. Only a single selected clip can have a selected action. Selecting an action is not an undo step and is not saved with the project.

### Edit an action's end state

While an action is selected, every field in the Clip tab shows and sets that action's **end state**, the values the clip reaches at the action's end. The same goes for the canvas: dragging the selected clip's handles, or nudging it with the arrow keys, writes the end state.

Unchecking a switch inside an action (a shadow or an outline, for example) turns that property off when the action ends.

The Clip tab marks each row so you can see what the action touches:

| Mark | Meaning |
|---|---|
| ◆ | This action animates the row. The label turns strong and the field gets a border in the action colour. A popup, checkbox or other on/off control also shows "at end", because it switches rather than ramps |
| ◇ | Another action on the clip animates this row. Its tooltip names the action |
| ○ | The row follows a value this action animates (for example, Gain follows Volume) |
| ⊘ | Actions don't animate this row. Edits change the clip |

A slider on an animated row fills in the action colour from the value at the action's start to the knob. When the playhead is inside the clip, a coral tick shows the value at the playhead. A row that is a field only shows that value as a "now …" tag instead.

Section headers carry the same marks, and a section where every row is ⊘ says "Actions don't animate this. Edits here change the clip." Each sub-tab's label shows **◆N** when the selected action animates N of its keys. When you select an action, the sections it animates on the current sub-tab open automatically.

To take a property back out of an action:

- Hover over a ◆ and click the × that replaces it ("Remove from action N").
- Click **Clear** in a section's header to remove all of that section's keys from the action. While an action is selected and keys the section, Clear takes the place of the header's **Reset**; otherwise Reset shows only while the section differs from its defaults.
- Right-click a row for its menu: **Remove from action N** on an animated row, **Go to action M** on a ◇ row (selects that action), and **Set end value to default** (on a row the selected action animates) or **Reset to default** (otherwise). The default item is disabled when the row already holds its default.

*Agents:* `set_action_end` (a `patch` with `video`, `audio`, `text` and `graphic` groups and a top-level `speed`, merged into the end state; `null` removes a key; `off` lists `"group.key"` paths to switch off at the end). `video.motion` and `text.words` are refused.

### Move, resize and re-curve an action

**In the action lane or the timeline:**

- Drag a band's **body** to move the action within its clip.
- Drag a band's outer 5 pt (its grips, shown on hover) to move that end. A band 15 pt wide or narrower has no grips and only moves.

A drag snaps to whole frames, keeps the action at least one frame long, and stops at the neighbouring actions and the clip's ends. A dashed outline marks where the band started. A readout replaces the lane's header text: "start → end +s:ff" for a move or a start resize, "len +Nf" for an end resize. The whole drag is one undo step (**Move Action** or **Resize Action**). Dropping the band selects the action. Bands don't snap to the playhead or other edits. If Frame Job would refuse a position, the band just stops there.

**In the action lane's detail row** (shown while an action is selected):

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| Start | Where the action starts, as a timecode measured from the clip's start |
| Length | How long it takes, 0.01–36000 s (quick picks 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2) |
| Curve | Linear, In, Out or In Out, with a glyph of the curve beside it |
| Trash button | Removes the action |

When Frame Job refuses a typed Start or Length, or an end-state edit, the reason appears at the foot of the inspector as "Refused: …" with the rule's own sentence. It stays until the project next changes or you click it. A band drag never shows one.

*Agents:* `set_action` (`start`, `duration`, `curve`; any left out keep their value).

### Remove an action

With an action selected, press **⌫**, or click the trash button in the action lane. ⌫ removes only the action, not the clip.

Careful: **⌘⌫** (Ripple Delete) still ripple-deletes the whole selected clip, even while an action is selected.

A speed action can't be removed if doing so would make the clip read past the end of its media. The refusal names the latest clip end that fits. See [Speed](speed.md).

*Agents:* `remove_action`.

### Actions on the timeline

Each clip that has an action shows an **action lane** directly under its name strip, with one band per action. How much a band shows depends on **View ▸ Timeline Track Height**:

| Track height | A band shows |
|---|---|
| Small | The bar only |
| Medium | Its number, a zoom glyph for a zoom action, and the curve on the selected band |
| Large | All of that, plus the properties it changes (for example `scale, x, y`, or `speed`) |

Actions are numbered in time order, and the number is the same on the timeline and in the Clip tab. The selected action's band is solid, a wash runs down the clip under its span, and the span is shaded on the ruler.

### The action lane in the Clip tab

The Clip tab opens with a pinned block above its sections: the selection header, the action lane, and the sub-tabs. The action lane is a small timeline of the selected clip:

- **Header row:** ACTIONS, then the count (or "none") and "· editing N" while action N is selected, then three buttons: Zoom to Region (Z), Zoom Back, and Add Action (⌥⌘K).
- **Lane row:** the **Clip** chip (highlighted while no action is selected; click it to leave the action), then the whole clip with its actions as numbered bands and the playhead. Under the bands the lane also shows the clip's transition overlap (hatched), its audio fades and its motion wedges, the same marks the timeline draws. An empty lane reads "no actions · ⌥⌘K adds one".
- **Detail row:** only while an action is selected (see above).

With several clips selected the lane reads "Select one clip to edit its actions."

### How edits move actions

| Edit | What happens to the clip's actions |
|---|---|
| Trim the start | Actions keep their clip time, so they stay put relative to the clip's new start |
| Trim the end | Actions stay put, so one can end up running past the clip's new end; only the part inside the clip plays. You can still move it earlier, shorten it or change its curve, but not make it end any later |
| Slip or Roll | Actions stay where they are in clip time |
| Change the speed, or rate-stretch | Actions keep their place as a fraction of the clip |
| Split | Actions after the cut go to the second half; one that spans the cut is divided between the halves |
| Add a transition at a hard cut | The incoming clip's actions move with its new first frame, so a zoom stays on the frame it was drawn over |
| Duplicate, Copy and Paste | The copies keep their actions |
| Nest | The clips keep their actions inside the nest |
| Detach Audio | The new audio clip gets a copy of every action, so volume actions keep working |
| Freeze Frame | The still has no actions; the look at the frozen frame is baked into its own properties |
| Add Blurred Background | The backdrop copy has no actions, so a zoom on the foreground doesn't zoom the backdrop |
| Paste Attributes | Actions are not copied |

13	    /// refusal — and neither is one on a locked track.

142	/// Retiming an action by drag (spec §11 CI-11, §6 `set_action`), the ONE
143	/// session the timeline's lane and the Clip tab's lane both drag with.
144	///
145	/// Everything here is CLIP time. Every tick sends start AND duration, frame
146	/// snapped, as one `set_action`; `ProjectDocument.updateLiveEdit` re-applies
147	/// it to the handle the gesture started from, so the ops never compound.
148	///
149	/// The clamp is a PREVIEW clamp, `TrimSession`'s kind: it mirrors the two
150	/// walls the core's refusals name — another action (`edit_action.rs`
151	/// `overlapping_action`, `start < o.end && o.start < end`, which makes a
152	/// zero-length action at the band's start or end a wall) and the clip's own
153	/// length — so the band stops where the core would refuse. It does not
154	/// replace the core's check; a tick the core still refuses is swallowed.
155	///
156	/// `originalDuration > 0` is an invariant both callers hold: a zero-length
157	/// action is never dragged, because `duration: 0` is invalid input to the
158	/// core (the `err_out` channel), not a refusal.
159	struct ActionDragSession {
160	    let clip: UInt32
161	    let action: UInt32
162	    let mode: ActionDragMode
163	    let originalStart: Ticks
164	    let originalDuration: Ticks
165	    /// Pointer clip time − `originalStart` at mouse-down, so the band keeps
166	    /// its place under the pointer instead of jumping to it.
167	    let grabOffset: Ticks
168	    /// One frame of the document's grid: the minimum length, the core's own.
169	    let frame: Ticks
170	    /// The latest end at or before `originalStart` among the clip's OTHER
171	    /// actions, or 0.
172	    let lowerWall: Ticks
173	    /// The earliest start at or after the original end among the clip's
174	    /// OTHER actions, or the clip's length floored to the frame grid.
175	    let upperWall: Ticks
176	    let fps: Fps
177	
178	    var start: Ticks
179	    var duration: Ticks
180	    /// False until the pointer moves — a press that only selects registers
181	    /// no undo step.
182	    var didMove = false
183	
184	    init(
185	        clip: ClipSnapshot, action: ActionSnapshot, mode: ActionDragMode, grabAt clipTime: Ticks,
186	        fps: Fps
187	    ) {
188	        self.clip = clip.id
189	        self.action = action.id
190	        self.mode = mode
191	        originalStart = action.start
192	        originalDuration = action.duration
193	        grabOffset = clipTime - action.start
194	        frame = max(fps.frameDuration, 1)
195	        self.fps = fps
196	        let end = action.endTime
197	        var lower: Ticks = 0
198	        // Floored: an off-grid length would let a clamped edge snap past it.
199	        // Never below the action's own end, or a move would clamp it left.
200	        var upper = max(clip.duration - clip.duration % frame, end)
201	        for other in ActionBands.ordered(clip) where other.id != action.id {
202	            if other.endTime <= action.start { lower = max(lower, other.endTime) }
203	            if other.start >= end { upper = min(upper, other.start) }
204	        }
205	        lowerWall = max(0, lower)
206	        upperWall = upper
207	        start = action.start
208	        duration = action.duration
209	    }
210	
211	    var endTime: Ticks { start + duration }
212	
213	    var changed: Bool { start != originalStart || duration != originalDuration }
214	
215	    var op: ReelOp { .setAction(clip: clip, action: action, start: start, duration: duration) }
216	
217	    var undoName: String { mode == .move ? "Move Action" : "Resize Action" }
218	
219	    /// `clipTime` is the pointer's clip time. The grabbed edge (both edges,
220	    /// for a move) travels by the pointer's travel, snapped to the frame
221	    /// grid, then clamped to the walls and the one-frame minimum.
222	    mutating func update(clipTime: Ticks) {
223	        let low = lowerWall, high = upperWall
224	        let travel = clipTime - (originalStart + grabOffset)
225	        let originalEnd = originalStart + originalDuration
226	        switch mode {
227	        case .move:
228	            let proposed = ReelTime.snapToFrame(originalStart + travel, fps: fps)
229	            start = max(min(proposed, high - originalDuration), low)
230	            duration = originalDuration
231	        case .resize(.start):
232	            let proposed = ReelTime.snapToFrame(originalStart + travel, fps: fps)
233	            start = max(min(proposed, originalEnd - frame), low)
234	            duration = originalEnd - start
235	        case .resize(.end):
236	            let proposed = ReelTime.snapToFrame(originalEnd + travel, fps: fps)
237	            let end = min(max(proposed, originalStart + frame), high)
238	            start = originalStart
239	            duration = end - originalStart
240	        }
241	        didMove = true
242	    }
243	
244	    /// The HUD's text. A move or a start resize: "new start → new end  +s:ff"
245	    /// (the start's offset, in seconds and frames); an end resize:
246	    /// "len +Nf". `base` turns clip time into the time the caller shows.
247	    func hud(base: Ticks, frames: Bool) -> String {
248	        if mode == .resize(.end) {
249	            let delta = (duration - originalDuration) / frame
250	            return "len \(delta < 0 ? "−" : "+")\(abs(delta))f"
251	        }
252	        let from = ReelTime.format(base + start, fps: fps, frames: frames)
253	        let to = ReelTime.format(base + endTime, fps: fps, frames: frames)
254	        let offset = start - originalStart
255	        let magnitude = abs(offset)
256	        let seconds = magnitude / ReelTime.perSecond
257	        let rest = (magnitude % ReelTime.perSecond) / frame
258	        let sign = offset < 0 ? "−" : "+"
259	        return "\(from) → \(to)  \(sign)\(seconds):\(rest < 10 ? "0" : "")\(rest)"
260	    }
261	}

302	/// What the timeline's action lane and the Clip tab's lane share (spec §11
303	/// CI-4): the ORDER actions are numbered in, the words a band's label is made
304	/// of, the zoom test, and the one painter both call — so a band on the
305	/// timeline and the same band in the inspector cannot disagree about its
306	/// number or its ink.
307	///
308	/// Drawn in a FLIPPED view: `minY` is the band's top. Everything here is
309	/// relative to the band it is handed; where the band sits is its caller's.
310	enum ActionBands {
311	    /// Time order — start, then id for two that share one (they cannot
312	    /// overlap, but a zero-length action can sit on another's start). An
313	    /// action's NUMBER is its index here plus one, everywhere.
314	    static func ordered(_ clip: ClipSnapshot) -> [ActionSnapshot] {
315	        clip.actions.sorted { ($0.start, $0.id) < ($1.start, $1.id) }
316	    }
317	
318	    /// Which properties an action changes — the end patch's keys, spelled
319	    /// the way the model spells them, sorted (what the old Actions table
320	    /// printed beside each curve); `speed` when the end names a rate (spec
321	    /// §11 SR-21 (d)).
322	    static func keys(of patch: ActionPatch) -> [String] {
323	        var keys: [String] = []
324	        if let video = patch.video { keys.append(contentsOf: video.dictionary.keys) }
325	        if let audio = patch.audio { keys.append(contentsOf: audio.dictionary.keys) }
326	        if let text = patch.text { keys.append(contentsOf: text.dictionary.keys) }
327	        if let graphic = patch.graphic { keys.append(contentsOf: graphic.props.keys) }
328	        if patch.speed != nil { keys.append("speed") }
329	        return keys.sorted()
330	    }

332	    /// A screencast zoom's shape — `add_zoom_action` writes exactly `scale`,
333	    /// `x` and `y` and nothing else, so an end patch of those three keys is
334	    /// drawn with the zoom glyph whichever door wrote it. An end naming a rate
335	    /// is not a zoom (spec §11 SR-21 (d)).
336	    static func isZoom(_ action: ActionSnapshot) -> Bool {
337	        let end = action.end
338	        guard let video = end.video, end.audio?.isEmpty ?? true, end.text?.isEmpty ?? true,
339	              end.graphic?.props.isEmpty ?? true, end.speed == nil
340	        else { return false }
341	        return Set(video.dictionary.keys) == ["scale", "x", "y"]
342	    }

344	    /// How much a band says, by track size: S bars only, M the number (and
345	    /// the zoom glyph and the selected band's curve), L the label too.
346	    enum Level {
347	        case bars, number, label
348	
349	        init(sizeIndex: Int) {
350	            switch sizeIndex {
351	            case ..<1: self = .bars
352	            case 1: self = .number

364	    static func gripEdge(in band: CGRect, at x: CGFloat) -> TimelineEdge? {
365	        guard band.width > grip * 3 else { return nil }

372	    /// hovered, 62 % with solid ends. Selected: solid, its text in
373	    /// `DS.actionInk`, and — from M — the curve as a 1.25 pt black-45 % line

377	    /// edge, so the band's bottom-right corner holds fill only (the proof

381	    static func draw(
382	        band: CGRect, number: Int, label: String?, curve: Curve?, zoom: Bool, selected: Bool,
383	        hovered: Bool, level: Level
384	    ) {
385	        guard band.width > 0, band.height > 0 else { return }
386	        NSGraphicsContext.current?.saveGraphicsState()
387	        NSBezierPath(rect: band).addClip()
388	        if selected {
389	            DS.action.setFill()

391	        } else {

393	            band.fill()

396	            NSRect(x: band.maxX - 1, y: band.minY, width: 1, height: band.height).fill()
397	        }
398	        defer {

402	                NSRect(x: band.minX, y: band.minY, width: grip, height: band.height).fill()

415	        let numberFont = DS.mono(9, weight: .semibold)
416	        let text = "\(number)"
417	        let numberWidth = ceil(text.size(withAttributes: [.font: numberFont]).width)
418	        var x = band.minX + 3
419	        TimelineDraw.truncated(
420	            text, in: CGRect(x: x, y: band.minY, width: numberWidth + 5, height: band.height),
421	            font: numberFont, color: ink)
422	        x += numberWidth + 2
423	        if zoom {
424	            TimelineDraw.symbol(

426	                in: CGRect(x: x, y: band.minY, width: 11, height: band.height), tint: ink)
427	            x += 11 + 2

429	        if level == .label, let label, !label.isEmpty {
430	            x += 2
431	            let room = CGRect(

438	    /// The easing as a line across `rect`: progress along x, the eased value
439	    /// up the rect (the view is flipped, so "up" is toward `minY`). The
440	    /// selected band strokes it, and so does the lane's `CurveGlyphView`.
441	    static func curvePath(_ curve: Curve, in rect: CGRect) -> NSBezierPath {
442	        let path = NSBezierPath()
443	        let steps = 16
444	        for step in 0...steps {
445	            let t = CGFloat(step) / CGFloat(steps)
446	            let point = CGPoint(
447	                x: rect.minX + t * rect.width, y: rect.maxY - eased(curve, t) * rect.height)
448	            if step == 0 { path.move(to: point) } else { path.line(to: point) }
449	        }
450	        return path
451	    }
452	
453	    /// A glyph's easing, not the core's: the shape reads as the curve, and no
454	    /// frame is computed from it.
455	    private static func eased(_ curve: Curve, _ t: CGFloat) -> CGFloat {
456	        switch curve {
457	        case .linear: return t
458	        case .easeIn: return t * t
459	        case .easeOut: return 1 - (1 - t) * (1 - t)
460	        case .easeInOut: return t < 0.5 ? 2 * t * t : 1 - 2 * (1 - t) * (1 - t)
461	        }
462	    }
463	}

866	/// Retiming an action by dragging its band in the Clip tab's lane (spec §11
867	/// CI-11) — the same `ActionDragSession` the timeline drags with, through the
868	/// binding's live trio, so a drag is ONE undo step.
869	///
870	/// The lane selects at mouse-UP, not at the press as the timeline does: a
871	/// selection rebuilds the pane, and the pane must not rebuild under the
872	/// pointer (`refresh(isLive:)` skips rebuilds only while a live edit runs).
873	/// A click and a drop therefore share one path, `releaseBand`.
874	extension ActionLaneView {
875	    /// The clip time under `x`: the lane's fraction of the clip's length,
876	    /// clamped to the clip.
877	    func clipTime(atX x: CGFloat) -> Ticks {
878	        guard let clip = clip, clip.duration > 0 else { return 0 }
879	        let lane = laneRect
880	        guard lane.width > 0 else { return 0 }
881	        let fraction = min(max((x - lane.minX) / lane.width, 0), 1)
882	        return Ticks((Double(fraction) * Double(clip.duration)).rounded())
883	    }
884	
885	    /// The band under `point` and the grip it is in, if any. The LAST band
886	    /// holding the point wins, because bands paint in time order and that is
887	    /// the one on top — so a zero-length band sitting on another's start is
888	    /// the one a press takes. A zero-length band answers too (it is
889	    /// selectable), always with no edge: 2 pt is all body.
890	    func bandHit(at point: CGPoint) -> ActionBandHover? {
891	        guard let clipID, let band = bandRects().last(where: { $0.rect.contains(point) })
892	        else { return nil }
893	        return ActionBandHover(
894	            clip: clipID, action: band.id, edge: ActionBands.gripEdge(in: band.rect, at: point.x))
895	    }
896	
897	    /// Mouse-down in the lane. True when a band was hit; it is remembered in
898	    /// `pressed`, and a session starts — with `liveBegin` — ONLY for an action
899	    /// with a length: `duration: 0` is invalid input to the core (the
900	    /// `err_out` channel), not a refusal, so a zero-length band is click to
901	    /// select and nothing else. Nothing is selected here (CI-11).
902	    func pressBand(at point: CGPoint) -> Bool {
903	        guard let hit = bandHit(at: point) else { return false }
904	        pressed = hit.action
905	        hover = nil
906	        guard let clip = clip, let action = clip.actions.first(where: { $0.id == hit.action }),
907	              action.duration > 0
908	        else { return true }
909	        drag = ActionDragSession(
910	            clip: clip, action: action, mode: hit.edge.map { .resize($0) } ?? .move,
911	            grabAt: clipTime(atX: point.x), fps: binding.canvas.fps)
912	        binding.liveBegin()
913	        return true
914	    }
915	
916	    /// Mouse-dragged: one `set_action` per tick; a refused tick is swallowed
917	    /// by `updateLiveEdit`.
918	    func dragBand(to point: CGPoint) {
919	        guard var session = drag else { return }
920	        session.update(clipTime: clipTime(atX: point.x))
921	        drag = session
922	        binding.liveUpdate([session.op])
923	        needsDisplay = true
924	    }
925	
926	    /// Mouse-up: the drag's one undo step, if there was a drag, then the
927	    /// pressed band selected — a click and a drop alike, which parks the
928	    /// playhead at the action's (new) end.
929	    func releaseBand() {
930	        let session = drag
931	        let id = pressed
932	        drag = nil
933	        pressed = nil
934	        if let session { binding.liveEnd(session.undoName) }
935	        if let id { binding.selectAction(id) }
936	        needsDisplay = true
937	    }

941	    /// One area of the lane's own (only areas it OWNS are removed —
942	    /// app/CLAUDE.md "Tracking areas").
943	    func installLaneTracking() {
944	        for area in trackingAreas where area.owner === self { removeTrackingArea(area) }
945	        addTrackingArea(
946	            NSTrackingArea(
947	                rect: .zero,
948	                options: [.mouseMoved, .mouseEnteredAndExited, .activeInKeyWindow, .inVisibleRect],
949	                owner: self, userInfo: nil))
950	    }

953	        guard drag == nil else {
954	            hover = nil
955	            return
956	        }
957	        hover = bandHit(at: convert(event.locationInWindow, from: nil))

962	    /// `.openHand` over a body, `.resizeLeftRight` over a grip — and nothing
963	    /// over a zero-length band, which a press will not move.
964	    func addBandCursorRects() {
965	        guard let clip = clip else { return }
966	        for band in bandRects() {
967	            guard let action = clip.actions.first(where: { $0.id == band.id }),
968	                  action.duration > 0
969	            else { continue }
970	            addGripCursorRects(band.rect)

972	    }

976	    /// While a drag has moved: the original band as a dashed ghost in the
977	    /// lane, and the HUD where the header row's text was (its buttons stay).
978	    /// The HUD's times are CLIP-relative, the detail row's Start field's.
979	    func drawDragOverlay() {
980	        guard let session = drag, session.didMove, let clip = clip, clip.duration > 0 else {
981	            return
982	        }
983	        let lane = laneRect
984	        let span = CGFloat(clip.duration)
985	        let from = lane.minX + lane.width * CGFloat(session.originalStart) / span
986	        let to = lane.minX + lane.width
987	            * CGFloat(session.originalStart + session.originalDuration) / span
988	        ActionDragSession.drawGhost(
989	            CGRect(x: from, y: lane.minY + 4, width: max(to - from, 2), height: lane.height - 8))
990	        let text = session.hud(base: 0, frames: binding.canvas.timecodeFrames)
991	        ActionDragSession.drawHUD(
992	            text,
993	            at: CGPoint(
994	                x: Self.side, y: Self.top + (Self.headerRow - ActionDragSession.hudHeight) / 2))

1012	    /// `lane` is the whole clip, start to end; every width is a fraction of
1013	    /// the clip's length, at least 2 pt and never wider than the lane.
1014	    func decor(_ clip: ClipSnapshot, in lane: CGRect) -> ActionLaneDecor {
1015	        var decor = ActionLaneDecor()
1016	        guard clip.duration > 0, lane.width > 0, lane.height > 0 else { return decor }
1017	        let snapshot = binding.snapshot
1018	        func width(_ ticks: Ticks) -> CGFloat {
1019	            min(max(lane.width * CGFloat(ticks) / CGFloat(clip.duration), 2), lane.width)
1020	        }
1021	        // `drawTransition`'s gate: a transition, over a predecessor that
1022	        // still runs when this clip starts.
1023	        if clip.transitionIn != nil,
1024	           let previous = snapshot.clips(onTrack: clip.track).last(where: {
1025	               $0.start < clip.start
1026	           }),
1027	           previous.end > clip.start
1028	        {
1029	            decor.hatch = CGRect(
1030	                x: lane.minX, y: lane.minY, width: width(previous.end - clip.start),
1031	                height: lane.height)
1032	        }
1033	        if InspectorTab.hasAudio(clip, in: snapshot) {
1034	            let audio = clip.audioProps
1035	            let tall = min(10, lane.height)
1036	            if audio.fadeIn > 0 {
1037	                decor.fadeIn = CGRect(
1038	                    x: lane.minX, y: lane.maxY - tall, width: width(audio.fadeIn), height: tall)
1039	            }
1040	            if audio.fadeOut > 0 {
1041	                let w = width(audio.fadeOut)
1042	                decor.fadeOut = CGRect(
1043	                    x: lane.maxX - w, y: lane.maxY - tall, width: w, height: tall)
1044	            }
1045	        }
1046	        // `drawNameStrip`'s gate, and `drawMotionWedges`' length: the EDGE's.
1047	        if InspectorTab.hasPixels(clip, in: snapshot), let motion = clip.videoProps.motion {
1048	            let tall = min(8, lane.height)
1049	            if let edge = motion.inEdge, edge.isActive {
1050	                decor.wedgeIn = CGRect(
1051	                    x: lane.minX, y: lane.minY, width: width(edge.duration), height: tall)
1052	            }
1053	            if let edge = motion.out, edge.isActive {
1054	                let w = width(edge.duration)
1055	                decor.wedgeOut = CGRect(x: lane.maxX - w, y: lane.minY, width: w, height: tall)
1056	            }
1057	        }
1058	        return decor
1059	    }
1060	
1061	    /// The decor, drawn in the well before the bands: the hatch (white 26 %,
1062	    /// the timeline's 3 pt on a 7 pt perpendicular period) with a 1 pt
1063	    /// white-40 % right edge; each fade a right triangle along the bottom,
1064	    /// rising toward the clip's inside, at white 16 % (the handoff's shape);
1065	    /// each wedge a triangle hanging from the top, deepest at the clip's
1066	    /// edge, in `DS.textFaint`.
1067	    func drawDecor(_ clip: ClipSnapshot, in lane: CGRect) {
1068	        let decor = decor(clip, in: lane)
1069	        NSGraphicsContext.current?.saveGraphicsState()
1070	        NSBezierPath(rect: lane).addClip()
1071	        if let hatch = decor.hatch {
1072	            TimelineDraw.hatch(
1073	                hatch, color: NSColor.white.withAlphaComponent(0.26),
1074	                spacing: 7 * 2.0.squareRoot(), lineWidth: 3)
1075	            NSColor.white.withAlphaComponent(0.4).setFill()
1076	            NSRect(x: hatch.maxX - 1, y: hatch.minY, width: 1, height: hatch.height).fill()
1077	        }
1078	        NSColor.white.withAlphaComponent(0.16).setFill()
1079	        if let fade = decor.fadeIn {
1080	            triangle(fade.minX, fade.maxY, fade.maxX, fade.maxY, fade.maxX, fade.minY)
1081	        }
1082	        if let fade = decor.fadeOut {
1083	            triangle(fade.maxX, fade.maxY, fade.minX, fade.maxY, fade.minX, fade.minY)
1084	        }
1085	        DS.textFaint.setFill()
1086	        if let wedge = decor.wedgeIn {
1087	            triangle(wedge.minX, wedge.minY, wedge.maxX, wedge.minY, wedge.minX, wedge.maxY)
1088	        }
1089	        if let wedge = decor.wedgeOut {
1090	            triangle(wedge.maxX, wedge.minY, wedge.minX, wedge.minY, wedge.maxX, wedge.maxY)
1091	        }
1092	        NSGraphicsContext.current?.restoreGraphicsState()
1093	    }

1095	    private func triangle(
1096	        _ x0: CGFloat, _ y0: CGFloat, _ x1: CGFloat, _ y1: CGFloat, _ x2: CGFloat, _ y2: CGFloat
1097	    ) {
1098	        let path = NSBezierPath()
1099	        path.move(to: CGPoint(x: x0, y: y0))
1100	        path.line(to: CGPoint(x: x1, y: y1))
1101	        path.line(to: CGPoint(x: x2, y: y2))
1102	        path.close()
1103	        path.fill()
1104	    }
1105	}

1175	    /// document's `selectAction` then overrules.

1177	        guard let document = document,
1178	              let snapshot = document.editedProject.snapshot.clip(clip),

1180	        else {

3	/// Retiming an action by dragging its band on the timeline (spec §11
4	/// CI-11): the begin/continue/end bodies, the hover, the cursors and the
5	/// ghost with its HUD. `TimelineView.swift` is frozen at wiring
6	/// (app/CLAUDE.md), so it keeps the stored `actionDrag` and `bandHover`, one
7	/// arm per gesture phase, a draw call, a cursor call and three one-line
8	/// overrides; the bodies are here.
9	extension TimelineView {
10	    /// Mouse-down on a band, after the press has selected the clip and the
11	    /// action (the timeline selects at mouse-DOWN). A zero-length action is
12	    /// never dragged — `duration: 0` is invalid input to the core, not a
13	    /// refusal — and neither is one on a locked track.
14	    func beginActionDrag(clip id: UInt32, action: UInt32, mode: ActionDragMode, at point: CGPoint) {
15	        guard let clip = snapshot.clip(id),
16	              let index = snapshot.trackIndex(of: clip.track),
17	              !snapshot.tracks[index].locked,
18	              let found = clip.actions.first(where: { $0.id == action }),
19	              found.duration > 0
20	        else { return }
21	        bandHover = nil
22	        actionDrag = ActionDragSession(
23	            clip: clip, action: found, mode: mode,
24	            grabAt: layout.time(atX: point.x) - clip.start, fps: snapshot.canvas.fps)
25	        onLiveBegin?()
26	    }
27	
28	    /// Mouse-dragged: one `set_action` per tick. A tick the core refuses is
29	    /// swallowed by `updateLiveEdit` (spec §11 CI-10's last sentence).
30	    func continueActionDrag(at point: CGPoint) {
31	        guard var session = actionDrag, let clip = snapshot.clip(session.clip) else { return }
32	        session.update(clipTime: layout.time(atX: point.x) - clip.start)
33	        actionDrag = session
34	        onLiveUpdate?([session.op])
35	    }
36	
37	    /// Mouse-up: the gesture as ONE undo step (none when nothing applied),
38	    /// then — after a real drag — the action selected again, which parks the
39	    /// playhead at its NEW end.
40	    func endActionDrag() {
41	        guard let session = actionDrag else { return }
42	        actionDrag = nil
43	        onLiveEnd?(session.undoName)
44	        if session.didMove { onActionSelected?(session.clip, session.action) }
45	    }
46	}

50	    /// removed (app/CLAUDE.md "Tracking areas"), and `.inVisibleRect` means a
51	    /// scroll needs no reinstall.

54	        addTrackingArea(

58	                owner: self, userInfo: nil))

62	    /// is live.

127	/// What a press on a band grabbed: its body, or one of its outer 5 pt.
128	enum ActionDragMode: Equatable {
129	    case move
130	    case resize(TimelineEdge)
131	}
132	
133	/// The band under the pointer while nothing is pressed — which band, and
134	/// which grip when it is over one. Both lanes keep one, and `ActionBands.draw`
135	/// paints its hover arm and grips from it (spec §11 CI-11).
136	struct ActionBandHover: Equatable {
137	    let clip: UInt32
138	    let action: UInt32
139	    let edge: TimelineEdge?
140	}
141	
142	/// Retiming an action by drag (spec §11 CI-11, §6 `set_action`), the ONE
143	/// session the timeline's lane and the Clip tab's lane both drag with.
144	///
145	/// Everything here is CLIP time. Every tick sends start AND duration, frame
146	/// snapped, as one `set_action`; `ProjectDocument.updateLiveEdit` re-applies
147	/// it to the handle the gesture started from, so the ops never compound.
148	///
149	/// The clamp is a PREVIEW clamp, `TrimSession`'s kind: it mirrors the two
150	/// walls the core's refusals name — another action (`edit_action.rs`
151	/// `overlapping_action`, `start < o.end && o.start < end`, which makes a
152	/// zero-length action at the band's start or end a wall) and the clip's own
153	/// length — so the band stops where the core would refuse. It does not
154	/// replace the core's check; a tick the core still refuses is swallowed.
155	///
156	/// `originalDuration > 0` is an invariant both callers hold: a zero-length
157	/// action is never dragged, because `duration: 0` is invalid input to the
158	/// core (the `err_out` channel), not a refusal.
159	struct ActionDragSession {
160	    let clip: UInt32
161	    let action: UInt32
162	    let mode: ActionDragMode
163	    let originalStart: Ticks
164	    let originalDuration: Ticks
165	    /// Pointer clip time − `originalStart` at mouse-down, so the band keeps
166	    /// its place under the pointer instead of jumping to it.
167	    let grabOffset: Ticks
168	    /// One frame of the document's grid: the minimum length, the core's own.
169	    let frame: Ticks
170	    /// The latest end at or before `originalStart` among the clip's OTHER
171	    /// actions, or 0.
172	    let lowerWall: Ticks
173	    /// The earliest start at or after the original end among the clip's
174	    /// OTHER actions, or the clip's length floored to the frame grid.
175	    let upperWall: Ticks
176	    let fps: Fps
177	
178	    var start: Ticks
179	    var duration: Ticks
180	    /// False until the pointer moves — a press that only selects registers
181	    /// no undo step.
182	    var didMove = false
183	
184	    init(
185	        clip: ClipSnapshot, action: ActionSnapshot, mode: ActionDragMode, grabAt clipTime: Ticks,
186	        fps: Fps
187	    ) {
188	        self.clip = clip.id
189	        self.action = action.id
190	        self.mode = mode
191	        originalStart = action.start
192	        originalDuration = action.duration
193	        grabOffset = clipTime - action.start
194	        frame = max(fps.frameDuration, 1)
195	        self.fps = fps
196	        let end = action.endTime
197	        var lower: Ticks = 0
198	        // Floored: an off-grid length would let a clamped edge snap past it.
199	        // Never below the action's own end, or a move would clamp it left.
200	        var upper = max(clip.duration - clip.duration % frame, end)
201	        for other in ActionBands.ordered(clip) where other.id != action.id {
202	            if other.endTime <= action.start { lower = max(lower, other.endTime) }
203	            if other.start >= end { upper = min(upper, other.start) }
204	        }
205	        lowerWall = max(0, lower)
206	        upperWall = upper
207	        start = action.start
208	        duration = action.duration
209	    }
210	
211	    var endTime: Ticks { start + duration }
212	
213	    var changed: Bool { start != originalStart || duration != originalDuration }
214	
215	    var op: ReelOp { .setAction(clip: clip, action: action, start: start, duration: duration) }
216	
217	    var undoName: String { mode == .move ? "Move Action" : "Resize Action" }
218	
219	    /// `clipTime` is the pointer's clip time. The grabbed edge (both edges,
220	    /// for a move) travels by the pointer's travel, snapped to the frame
221	    /// grid, then clamped to the walls and the one-frame minimum.
222	    mutating func update(clipTime: Ticks) {
223	        let low = lowerWall, high = upperWall
224	        let travel = clipTime - (originalStart + grabOffset)
225	        let originalEnd = originalStart + originalDuration
226	        switch mode {
227	        case .move:
228	            let proposed = ReelTime.snapToFrame(originalStart + travel, fps: fps)
229	            start = max(min(proposed, high - originalDuration), low)
230	            duration = originalDuration
231	        case .resize(.start):
232	            let proposed = ReelTime.snapToFrame(originalStart + travel, fps: fps)
233	            start = max(min(proposed, originalEnd - frame), low)
234	            duration = originalEnd - start
235	        case .resize(.end):
236	            let proposed = ReelTime.snapToFrame(originalEnd + travel, fps: fps)
237	            let end = min(max(proposed, originalStart + frame), high)
238	            start = originalStart
239	            duration = end - originalStart
240	        }
241	        didMove = true
242	    }
243	
244	    /// The HUD's text. A move or a start resize: "new start → new end  +s:ff"
245	    /// (the start's offset, in seconds and frames); an end resize:
246	    /// "len +Nf". `base` turns clip time into the time the caller shows.
247	    func hud(base: Ticks, frames: Bool) -> String {
248	        if mode == .resize(.end) {
249	            let delta = (duration - originalDuration) / frame
250	            return "len \(delta < 0 ? "−" : "+")\(abs(delta))f"
251	        }
252	        let from = ReelTime.format(base + start, fps: fps, frames: frames)
253	        let to = ReelTime.format(base + endTime, fps: fps, frames: frames)
254	        let offset = start - originalStart
255	        let magnitude = abs(offset)
256	        let seconds = magnitude / ReelTime.perSecond
257	        let rest = (magnitude % ReelTime.perSecond) / frame
258	        let sign = offset < 0 ? "−" : "+"
259	        return "\(from) → \(to)  \(sign)\(seconds):\(rest < 10 ? "0" : "")\(rest)"
260	    }
261	}

302	/// What the timeline's action lane and the Clip tab's lane share (spec §11
303	/// CI-4): the ORDER actions are numbered in, the words a band's label is made
304	/// of, the zoom test, and the one painter both call — so a band on the
305	/// timeline and the same band in the inspector cannot disagree about its
306	/// number or its ink.
307	///
308	/// Drawn in a FLIPPED view: `minY` is the band's top. Everything here is
309	/// relative to the band it is handed; where the band sits is its caller's.
310	enum ActionBands {
311	    /// Time order — start, then id for two that share one (they cannot
312	    /// overlap, but a zero-length action can sit on another's start). An
313	    /// action's NUMBER is its index here plus one, everywhere.
314	    static func ordered(_ clip: ClipSnapshot) -> [ActionSnapshot] {
315	        clip.actions.sorted { ($0.start, $0.id) < ($1.start, $1.id) }
316	    }
317	
318	    /// Which properties an action changes — the end patch's keys, spelled
319	    /// the way the model spells them, sorted (what the old Actions table
320	    /// printed beside each curve); `speed` when the end names a rate (spec
321	    /// §11 SR-21 (d)).
322	    static func keys(of patch: ActionPatch) -> [String] {
323	        var keys: [String] = []
324	        if let video = patch.video { keys.append(contentsOf: video.dictionary.keys) }
325	        if let audio = patch.audio { keys.append(contentsOf: audio.dictionary.keys) }
326	        if let text = patch.text { keys.append(contentsOf: text.dictionary.keys) }
327	        if let graphic = patch.graphic { keys.append(contentsOf: graphic.props.keys) }
328	        if patch.speed != nil { keys.append("speed") }
329	        return keys.sorted()
330	    }
331	
332	    /// A screencast zoom's shape — `add_zoom_action` writes exactly `scale`,
333	    /// `x` and `y` and nothing else, so an end patch of those three keys is
334	    /// drawn with the zoom glyph whichever door wrote it. An end naming a rate
335	    /// is not a zoom (spec §11 SR-21 (d)).
336	    static func isZoom(_ action: ActionSnapshot) -> Bool {
337	        let end = action.end
338	        guard let video = end.video, end.audio?.isEmpty ?? true, end.text?.isEmpty ?? true,
339	              end.graphic?.props.isEmpty ?? true, end.speed == nil
340	        else { return false }
341	        return Set(video.dictionary.keys) == ["scale", "x", "y"]
342	    }
343	
344	    /// How much a band says, by track size: S bars only, M the number (and
345	    /// the zoom glyph and the selected band's curve), L the label too.
346	    enum Level {
347	        case bars, number, label
348	
349	        init(sizeIndex: Int) {
350	            switch sizeIndex {
351	            case ..<1: self = .bars
352	            case 1: self = .number
353	            default: self = .label
354	            }
355	        }
356	    }
357	
358	    /// The resize zone at each end of a band (spec §11 CI-11): its outer
359	    /// 5 pt, on a band wide enough to hold two of them and a body.
360	    static let grip: CGFloat = 5
361	
362	    /// Which end of `band` the x falls in the grip of, or nil for the body —
363	    /// always nil on a band 15 pt wide or less, which is all body.
364	    static func gripEdge(in band: CGRect, at x: CGFloat) -> TimelineEdge? {
365	        guard band.width > grip * 3 else { return nil }
366	        if x - band.minX <= grip { return .start }
367	        if band.maxX - x <= grip { return .end }
368	        return nil
369	    }
370	
371	    /// One band. Normal: the action ink at 34 % with 1 pt ends at 75 %;
372	    /// hovered, 62 % with solid ends. Selected: solid, its text in
373	    /// `DS.actionInk`, and — from M — the curve as a 1.25 pt black-45 % line
374	    /// from the bottom-left corner to the top-right, unless `curve` is nil
375	    /// (a Speed band under the rate line, `RateGraph.bandCurve`, spec §11
376	    /// SR-26). The number, the glyph and the label run from the LEADING
377	    /// edge, so the band's bottom-right corner holds fill only (the proof
378	    /// samples it there). Hovered, a band wide enough to resize draws its two
379	    /// 5 pt grips last — white 80 %, or black 45 % on the selected band — so
380	    /// an unhovered band never has them (CI-11).
381	    static func draw(
382	        band: CGRect, number: Int, label: String?, curve: Curve?, zoom: Bool, selected: Bool,
383	        hovered: Bool, level: Level
384	    ) {
385	        guard band.width > 0, band.height > 0 else { return }
386	        NSGraphicsContext.current?.saveGraphicsState()
387	        NSBezierPath(rect: band).addClip()
388	        if selected {
389	            DS.action.setFill()
390	            band.fill()
391	        } else {
392	            DS.action.withAlphaComponent(hovered ? 0.62 : 0.34).setFill()
393	            band.fill()
394	            DS.action.withAlphaComponent(hovered ? 1 : 0.75).setFill()
395	            NSRect(x: band.minX, y: band.minY, width: 1, height: band.height).fill()
396	            NSRect(x: band.maxX - 1, y: band.minY, width: 1, height: band.height).fill()
397	        }
398	        defer {
399	            if hovered, band.width > grip * 3 {
400	                (selected ? NSColor.black.withAlphaComponent(0.45)
401	                    : NSColor.white.withAlphaComponent(0.8)).setFill()
402	                NSRect(x: band.minX, y: band.minY, width: grip, height: band.height).fill()
403	                NSRect(x: band.maxX - grip, y: band.minY, width: grip, height: band.height).fill()
404	            }
405	            NSGraphicsContext.current?.restoreGraphicsState()
406	        }
407	        guard level != .bars else { return }
408	        if selected, let curve {
409	            let path = curvePath(curve, in: band)
410	            path.lineWidth = 1.25
411	            NSColor.black.withAlphaComponent(0.45).setStroke()
412	            path.stroke()
413	        }
414	        let ink = selected ? DS.actionInk : NSColor.white
415	        let numberFont = DS.mono(9, weight: .semibold)
416	        let text = "\(number)"
417	        let numberWidth = ceil(text.size(withAttributes: [.font: numberFont]).width)
418	        var x = band.minX + 3
419	        TimelineDraw.truncated(
420	            text, in: CGRect(x: x, y: band.minY, width: numberWidth + 5, height: band.height),
421	            font: numberFont, color: ink)
422	        x += numberWidth + 2
423	        if zoom {
424	            TimelineDraw.symbol(
425	                "plus.magnifyingglass", fallback: "+",
426	                in: CGRect(x: x, y: band.minY, width: 11, height: band.height), tint: ink)
427	            x += 11 + 2
428	        }
429	        if level == .label, let label, !label.isEmpty {
430	            x += 2
431	            let room = CGRect(
432	                x: x, y: band.minY, width: max(band.maxX - 3 - x, 0), height: band.height)
433	            TimelineDraw.truncated(
434	                label, in: room, font: DS.sans(10, weight: .semibold), color: ink)
435	        }
436	    }
437	
438	    /// The easing as a line across `rect`: progress along x, the eased value
439	    /// up the rect (the view is flipped, so "up" is toward `minY`). The
440	    /// selected band strokes it, and so does the lane's `CurveGlyphView`.
441	    static func curvePath(_ curve: Curve, in rect: CGRect) -> NSBezierPath {
442	        let path = NSBezierPath()
443	        let steps = 16
444	        for step in 0...steps {
445	            let t = CGFloat(step) / CGFloat(steps)
446	            let point = CGPoint(
447	                x: rect.minX + t * rect.width, y: rect.maxY - eased(curve, t) * rect.height)
448	            if step == 0 { path.move(to: point) } else { path.line(to: point) }
449	        }
450	        return path
451	    }
452	
453	    /// A glyph's easing, not the core's: the shape reads as the curve, and no
454	    /// frame is computed from it.
455	    private static func eased(_ curve: Curve, _ t: CGFloat) -> CGFloat {
456	        switch curve {
457	        case .linear: return t
458	        case .easeIn: return t * t
459	        case .easeOut: return 1 - (1 - t) * (1 - t)
460	        case .easeInOut: return t < 0.5 ? 2 * t * t : 1 - 2 * (1 - t) * (1 - t)
461	        }
462	    }
463	}

1014	    func decor(_ clip: ClipSnapshot, in lane: CGRect) -> ActionLaneDecor {
1015	        var decor = ActionLaneDecor()
1016	        guard clip.duration > 0, lane.width > 0, lane.height > 0 else { return decor }
1017	        let snapshot = binding.snapshot
1018	        func width(_ ticks: Ticks) -> CGFloat {
1019	            min(max(lane.width * CGFloat(ticks) / CGFloat(clip.duration), 2), lane.width)
1020	        }
1021	        // `drawTransition`'s gate: a transition, over a predecessor that
1022	        // still runs when this clip starts.
1023	        if clip.transitionIn != nil,
1024	           let previous = snapshot.clips(onTrack: clip.track).last(where: {
1025	               $0.start < clip.start
1026	           }),
1027	           previous.end > clip.start
1028	        {
1029	            decor.hatch = CGRect(
1030	                x: lane.minX, y: lane.minY, width: width(previous.end - clip.start),
1031	                height: lane.height)

1034	            let audio = clip.audioProps
1035	            let tall = min(10, lane.height)
1036	            if audio.fadeIn > 0 {

1038	                    x: lane.minX, y: lane.maxY - tall, width: width(audio.fadeIn), height: tall)
1039	            }
1040	            if audio.fadeOut > 0 {
1041	                let w = width(audio.fadeOut)
1042	                decor.fadeOut = CGRect(
1043	                    x: lane.maxX - w, y: lane.maxY - tall, width: w, height: tall)
1044	            }
1045	        }
1046	        // `drawNameStrip`'s gate, and `drawMotionWedges`' length: the EDGE's.
1047	        if InspectorTab.hasPixels(clip, in: snapshot), let motion = clip.videoProps.motion {
1048	            let tall = min(8, lane.height)
1049	            if let edge = motion.inEdge, edge.isActive {
1050	                decor.wedgeIn = CGRect(
1051	                    x: lane.minX, y: lane.minY, width: width(edge.duration), height: tall)
1052	            }
1053	            if let edge = motion.out, edge.isActive {
1054	                let w = width(edge.duration)
1055	                decor.wedgeOut = CGRect(x: lane.maxX - w, y: lane.minY, width: w, height: tall)

1063	    /// white-40 % right edge; each fade a right triangle along the bottom,
1064	    /// rising toward the clip's inside, at white 16 % (the handoff's shape);
1065	    /// each wedge a triangle hanging from the top, deepest at the clip's
1066	    /// edge, in `DS.textFaint`.

1068	        let decor = decor(clip, in: lane)
1069	        NSGraphicsContext.current?.saveGraphicsState()
1070	        NSBezierPath(rect: lane).addClip()
1071	        if let hatch = decor.hatch {
1072	            TimelineDraw.hatch(
1073	                hatch, color: NSColor.white.withAlphaComponent(0.26),
1074	                spacing: 7 * 2.0.squareRoot(), lineWidth: 3)
1075	            NSColor.white.withAlphaComponent(0.4).setFill()
1076	            NSRect(x: hatch.maxX - 1, y: hatch.minY, width: 1, height: hatch.height).fill()
1077	        }
1078	        NSColor.white.withAlphaComponent(0.16).setFill()
1079	        if let fade = decor.fadeIn {
1080	            triangle(fade.minX, fade.maxY, fade.maxX, fade.maxY, fade.maxX, fade.minY)
1081	        }
1082	        if let fade = decor.fadeOut {
1083	            triangle(fade.maxX, fade.maxY, fade.minX, fade.maxY, fade.minX, fade.minY)
1084	        }
1085	        DS.textFaint.setFill()
1086	        if let wedge = decor.wedgeIn {
1087	            triangle(wedge.minX, wedge.minY, wedge.maxX, wedge.minY, wedge.minX, wedge.maxY)

1089	        if let wedge = decor.wedgeOut {

---
title: Set what an action animates to
description: With an action selected, use the Clip tab or the canvas to set where a clip ends up, read the marks that show what the action changes, and take a property back out.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

An [action](/motion/actions/) moves a clip towards its end state: the values the clip reaches when the action finishes. A new action has an empty end state, so it changes nothing until you say what it animates to.

<AtAGlance
  where={[
    'Clip tab, with an action selected',
    'The canvas, with an action selected',
    'Right-click a row in the Clip tab',
  ]}
  tools="set_action_end"
/>

<Shot
  name="07b-clip-graphic-action.inspector"
  alt="The Clip tab with action 1 selected on a graphic clip. The Actions header reads editing 1. The Graphic sub-tab shows a count of 3, and so does the Properties section, which has a Clear button. The accent, size and boxed rows each have a diamond in their left gutter. The size slider has a coloured fill and a coral tick, its field has a coloured border, and boxed says at end. The Size and Timeline sections show the ⊘ mark."
/>

## Edit the end state

<Steps>

1. [Select the action](/motion/select-an-action/). Clicking its band also moves the playhead to the action's end, so the preview shows the state you're editing.

2. Change any row in the Clip tab. Type a value, drag a slider, pick from a pop-up or choose a colour.

3. Move the playhead through the action, or play it, to see the clip travel to what you set.

</Steps>

While an action is selected, every field shows the value the clip reaches at the action's end, and every edit writes that value. Changing a row adds it to the action, and the row gets a ◆.

Your edits follow the selected action, not the playhead. If the playhead wanders out of the action's span, the action stays selected and the fields keep showing its end.

To edit the clip itself again, press <kbd>Esc</kbd> or click the **Clip** chip at the start of the action lane.

What happens along the way depends on the kind of value. Numbers and most colours ramp along the action's curve, and switches, pop-ups and text hold and then change at the end. See [Actions](/motion/actions/).

## Edit on the canvas

With an action selected, the canvas writes the end state too. Moving, scaling, rotating or cropping the clip, nudging it with the arrow keys, dragging a text clip's wrap width and dragging an obscure region all change that action's end, not the clip.

The box on screen still shows the frame at the playhead, while a drag starts from the end state and changes it by the distance you drag. With the playhead partway through the action, the box moves only part of the way. Work with the playhead at the action's end, which is where clicking the band puts it, and the box lands where you let go.

Two things on the canvas always edit the clip itself:

- A drag on a multi-clip selection. Only a single selected clip can have a selected action.
- Resizing a shape's box, or dragging a line's or arrow's end points. A shape's own properties can't animate. Moving a shape still writes the action's end.

## Switch a property off

Untick a switch inside an action and that property turns off when the action ends. **Drop shadow**, a text clip's **Outline** and **Backdrop**, and sound switches such as **Limit peaks** all work this way, and so does a single band of the EQ.

The property stays on for the whole action, then goes off at its last moment. The row shows ◆ and "at end".

This is different from [taking the row out of the action](#take-a-property-out-of-the-action), which stops the action changing the property at all.

## Read the row marks

Each row in the Clip tab has a narrow gutter to the left of its label. The mark there says how the row relates to the selected action.

| Mark | What it means | How else you can tell |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ◆ | This action animates the row. | The label turns strong, and a field or pop-up gets a border in the action colour. |
| ◇ | Another action on the clip animates the row. | Its tooltip reads "Changed by action N". |
| ○ | The row follows a value this action animates. **Gain** follows **Volume**, for example. | |
| ⊘ | Actions don't animate this row, so an edit here changes the clip. | The label turns faint. |

A blank gutter means the row can animate and nothing is animating it yet.

◇ also shows when no action is selected, on every row an action on the clip animates. It's a quick way to see what's moving before you pick an action.

The **Normalize** button changes the clip whatever is selected. While an action is selected it carries a small boxed **clip** tag, and its tooltip reads "Actions don't animate this. It changes the clip."

### The "at end" tag

A control that can't blend says "at end" beside it once the action animates it. It holds its old value until the action ends, then switches.

Pop-ups, checkboxes, segmented controls and text fields all work this way. Most colours ramp, but a few can't blend, such as a cursor's ripple colour, and those say "at end" too.

## See the value change as it plays

The field always reads the value at the action's end. The rest of the row shows how it gets there.

**On a slider**, the rail fills in the action colour from the value at the action's start to the knob. A coral tick marks the value at the playhead. The tick shows whenever the playhead is inside the clip and that value differs from the knob, even with no action selected.

**On a row with no slider**, a coral tag gives that value in words, such as "now 1.50×". It shows while the playhead is inside the clip and the value there differs from the field.

## Read the sections and sub-tabs

Section headers carry the same marks as their rows:

- **◆N** counts what the selected action animates in that section.
- **◇** means another action animates a row in the section.
- **⊘** means every row in the section is ⊘, and the section also says "Actions don't animate this. Edits here change the clip."

The summary at the right of a header turns the action colour when the action animates the section.

### Sub-tab counts

Each sub-tab's label shows **◆N** when the selected action animates N things on it, so you can see what an action does without opening every tab.

| Sub-tab | What counts |
| --- | --- |
| Picture | Each property. A zoom action reads ◆3, for its scale and its two position values. |
| Color | Light and Color together count as one. Look, Wheels, Curves and Qualifier count as one each, however many values inside them change. On an adjustment clip, Strength counts as one too. |
| Sound | Each property. |
| Text | Each property. |
| Graphic | Each property the action animates. See [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/). |
| Clip | A speed change, as ◆1. See [Build a ramp by hand](/speed/build-a-ramp/). |
| Shape | Nothing, ever. A shape's own properties can't animate. |

### Sections open by themselves

Selecting an action opens the sections it animates on the sub-tab you're looking at, and they stay open for as long as that action is selected. A sub-tab you switch to later opens its own animated sections the first time it shows.

Close one by hand and it stays closed while that action is selected. None of this changes your own layout: leave the action and the sections go back to how you had them.

## Take a property out of the action

Taking a property out stops the action changing it. The row falls back to what the clip held before the action, and the action itself stays.

| To take out | Do this | Undo step |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One row | Hover over its ◆ and click the × that replaces it. The tooltip reads "Remove from action N". | Remove from Action |
| One row | Right-click it and choose **Remove from action N**. | Remove from Action |
| A whole section | Click **Clear** in the section's header. Its tooltip reads "Remove this section from action N". | Clear |
| Everything | [Remove the action](/motion/change-an-action/#remove-an-action). | Remove Action |

### Clear and Reset

**Clear** and **Reset** share one place in a section's header, and at most one of them shows.

- While an action is selected, a section with rows that can animate shows **Clear** if the action animates anything in it, and neither button if it doesn't.
- A section of ⊘ rows keeps **Reset**, because its edits go to the clip.
- With no action selected, **Reset** shows only while the section differs from its defaults.

## Right-click a row

Right-click a row's label, slider, checkbox or the space beside them. Each item shows only where it applies, and a row with nothing to offer has no menu. A text field or a pop-up keeps its own right-click menu.

| Item | When it shows | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Remove from action N** | The selected action animates the row | Takes the row out of the action. |
| **Go to action M** | The row shows ◇ | Selects the action that animates the row, and moves the playhead to that action's end. |
| **Set end value to default** | An action is selected, and the row can animate | Sets the value at the action's end to the row's default. |
| **Reset to default** | Any other row with a default | Puts the row back to its default. |

The two default items are greyed while the row already holds its default.

**Set end value to default** and **Remove from action N** aren't the same. The first makes the clip animate to the default. The second stops the action touching the row.

## Good to know

- Typing the number a field already shows isn't an edit, so it doesn't add the row to the action.
- Some rows always change the clip, whatever is selected, and they're marked ⊘. [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/) lists them.
- Adding or removing a filter or an obscure region changes the clip even inside an action, though dialling a value inside one animates. If the action already animates that list, the whole list then switches at the action's end rather than ramping.
- With several clips selected, the fields edit the clips themselves. The action lane reads "Select one clip to edit its actions."
- An end value Frame Job won't take shows the reason at the foot of the inspector. See [When an edit is refused](/motion/change-an-action/#when-an-edit-is-refused).
- Selecting an action isn't an undo step, but each change to its end state is.

## With an agent

`set_action_end` does what the fields do. It can also do one thing the fields can't: send a value past a row's usual range, which is only held to that range as the clip is drawn. A graphic's properties are the exception, and are checked when they're set. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/).

## Related

- [Actions](/motion/actions/)
- [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/)
- [Select an action](/motion/select-an-action/)
- [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/)
- [Animate sound with actions](/audio/animate-sound/)
- [Inspector fields](/getting-started/inspector-fields/)

Right-click a row's label, slider, checkbox or the space beside them. Each item shows only where it applies, and a row with nothing to offer has no menu. A text field or a pop-up keeps its own right-click menu.

| Item | When it shows | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Remove from action N** | The selected action animates the row | Takes the row out of the action. |
| **Go to action M** | The row shows ◇ | Selects the action that animates the row, and moves the playhead to that action's end. |
| **Set end value to default** | An action is selected, and the row can animate | Sets the value at the action's end to the row's default. |
| **Reset to default** | Any other row with a default | Puts the row back to its default. |

The two default items are greyed while the row already holds its default.

**Set end value to default** and **Remove from action N** aren't the same. The first makes the clip animate to the default. The second stops the action touching the row.

## Good to know

- Typing the number a field already shows isn't an edit, so it doesn't add the row to the action.
- Some rows always change the clip, whatever is selected, and they're marked ⊘. [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/) lists them.
- Adding or removing a filter or an obscure region changes the clip even inside an action, though dialling a value inside one animates. If the action already animates that list, the whole list then switches at the action's end rather than ramping.
- With several clips selected, the fields edit the clips themselves. The action lane reads "Select one clip to edit its actions."
- An end value Frame Job won't take shows the reason at the foot of the inspector. See [When an edit is refused](/motion/change-an-action/#when-an-edit-is-refused).
- Selecting an action isn't an undo step, but each change to its end state is.

## With an agent

`set_action_end` does what the fields do. It can also do one thing the fields can't: send a value past a row's usual range, which is only held to that range as the clip is drawn. A graphic's properties are the exception, and are checked when they're set. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/).

---
title: Move, resize or remove an action
description: Drag an action's band or type its Start, Length and Curve to change when it happens, or remove it and leave the clip in place.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

You can change when an [action](/motion/actions/) happens, how long it takes and how it eases, by dragging its band or typing in the action lane. Removing an action leaves the clip where it is.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Edit ▸ Delete"
  keys="⌫"
  where={['The action band on the timeline', 'Clip tab ▸ action lane']}
  tools={['set_action', 'remove_action']}
/>

<Shot
  name="10d-clip-speed-action.inspector"
  alt="The top of the Clip tab with action 1 selected. The lane shows the action's band across the middle of the clip. Under it, the detail row has a Start field reading 00:00:00:15, a Length field reading 1.00 s, a curve glyph, a Curve pop-up set to Linear and a trash button."
/>

## Move an action

Drag the body of a band, on the timeline or in the Clip tab's action lane, to move the action within its clip. The pointer is an open hand over the body, and a dashed outline marks where the band started.

When you let go, the action is selected and the playhead sits at its new end, or one frame short of it when the action ends with the clip. The whole drag is one undo step, **Move Action**.

## Resize an action

Drag either end of a band to move that end of the action. Each end's grip is its outer 5 pt. The grips appear when you hover over the band, and the pointer becomes a left-right arrow over them.

The action stays selected and the playhead goes to its new end, as with a move. The whole drag is one undo step, **Resize Action**.

A band 15 pt wide or narrower has no grips and only moves. [Zoom the timeline](/timeline/zoom-and-scroll/) in, or type a [length](#type-a-start-length-or-curve).

## Where a drag stops

A band drag snaps to whole frames and keeps the action at least one frame long. It stops at the neighbouring actions and at the clip's ends. It doesn't snap to the playhead or to other edits.

If Frame Job wouldn't allow a position, the band stops there and shows no message. A Speed action stops where the clip would read past the end of its media, for example.

An action that a trim left running past the clip's end can move earlier or get shorter, but can't end any later than it already does.

On the timeline, a band on a locked track doesn't drag. You can still select it.

## The drag readout

While you drag, a small readout gives the band's new place.

| You're dragging | The readout shows | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The body, or the start grip | The new start, the new end, and how far the start has moved in seconds and frames | `00:00:01:00 → 00:00:03:00  +0:12` |
| The end grip | How much the length has changed, in frames | `len −6f` |

On the timeline the readout floats above the clip and gives timeline times. In the Clip tab's lane it replaces the header text and gives times from the clip's own start, to match the Start field.

## Drag in the Clip tab's lane

The lane moves and resizes bands exactly as the timeline does, with the same limits and the same readout. It differs in two ways:

- It selects the action when you let go, where the timeline selects when you press. A click and a drop both select, and both move the playhead to the action's end.
- A locked track doesn't stop a drag here.

## Type a start, length or curve

The action lane's detail row shows while an action is selected.

| Control | What it does | Limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Start | Where the action starts, as a timecode from the clip's own start, not the timeline's. | Capped at the clip's length and snapped to a frame. |
| Length | How long the action takes, in seconds, with quick picks of 0.25, 0.5, 1 and 2. | 0.01 to 36000 s, then capped at the clip's length and snapped to a frame. |
| Curve | How the action eases from its start to its end state. A small glyph of the curve sits beside the pop-up. | **Linear**, **In**, **Out** or **In Out**. |
| Trash button | [Removes the action](#remove-an-action). | |

**Linear** runs at a constant speed. **In** starts slowly and ends fast, **Out** starts fast and ends slowly, and **In Out** is slow at both ends.

Each change is one undo step: **Move Action**, **Resize Action** or **Action Curve**.

A Start that isn't a timecode beeps and goes back to the old value. A Length under half a frame rounds to nothing, and Frame Job shows an error alert instead.

Length is capped at the whole clip, not at the room left after the action's start, so a long enough value can still run past the clip's end. That's one of the cases below.

## When an edit is refused

If Frame Job won't take a typed Start or Length, or an [end value](/motion/edit-an-action/), it beeps and shows the reason at the foot of the inspector, after "Refused: ". The message stays until the project next changes or you click it. See [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/) for how to read it.

| Frame Job won't do this when | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| The action would end past the clip's end, and later than it did before | Shorten it or move it earlier. |
| The action would overlap another action on the clip | Move or shorten one of them. |
| A Speed action would make the clip read past the end of its media | Use the latest clip end the message names. |
| The clip with a Speed action is linked to its sound | Choose **Attach Audio** first, as the message says. See [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/). |

A band drag never shows this message. The band stops instead.

## Remove an action

Select the action, then press <kbd>⌫</kbd>, choose **Edit ▸ Delete**, or click the trash button in the action lane. Only the action goes, as one undo step, **Remove Action**.

The clip keeps its own properties and loses what the action did to them.

A Speed action can't be removed if the clip would then read past the end of its media. The message names the latest clip end that fits. See [Build a ramp by hand](/speed/build-a-ramp/).

## Ripple Delete still deletes the clip

:::caution
<kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> (**Ripple Delete**) deletes the whole selected clip and closes the gap, even while an action is selected. Only <kbd>⌫</kbd> removes the action.
:::

## Good to know

- Moving, resizing or removing a Speed action re-times the captions on a Captions track that sit wholly inside a clip with sound, in the same undo step. The step's name gains "and Re-time Captions". See [Captions follow a speed change](/speed/captions-and-speed/).
- With words selected in the [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-tab/), <kbd>⌫</kbd> removes those words, not the action.
- A zero-length action draws as a band 2 pt wide. You can click it to select it, but it doesn't drag.
- Clicking a band on a clip in a multi-clip selection selects that clip alone.

## With an agent

`set_action` moves an action, changes its length or changes its curve in one step, and `remove_action` removes it. Where a band stops, an agent's edit that goes too far is refused with the same reason a typed value gets. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/).

## Related

- [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/)
- [Action bands and the action lane](/motion/action-lane/)
- [How edits move actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/)
- [Build a ramp by hand](/speed/build-a-ramp/)
